quality_gate: Confirm the current plan and target version before promoting a relationship.
Match indicator name, definition, unit, population, and component structure.
Keep target year, reporting year, measurement year, and fiscal year separate.
Keep budget, supplementary budget, execution, settlement, project cost, and contract amount separate.
Match project identity using policy measure, department, office, year, and normalized name.
Verify candidate, election, term, and original wording before linking an executive promise.
Treat assembly and audit evidence as separate accountability roles from executive outcomes.
Retain official URL, page, extraction position, review date, and unresolved boundary.
Do not promote automated extraction to linked without reviewed evidence.
Do not infer policy achievement, causality, or cross-prefecture comparability.

waves.objective: Unify the existing Hokkaido, Miyagi, Tokyo, and Fukuoka record-level implementations under one reusable contract.
exit_criteria: Four reference records validate against the shared Phase 11 schema.
Every reference resolves to an existing reviewed source record and evidence path.
Layer periods and money types remain separate without policy assessment.
waves.next_action: Expand the reference catalog beyond one representative record per prefecture and extract reusable promotion rules.

waves.objective: Create at least one reviewed record-level Evidence Chain or explicit maximum official-source depth for each remaining regional anchor.
exit_criteria: Each remaining anchor has a schema-valid record or explicit maximum-depth boundary.
Every promoted link passes the same version, period, organization, and evidence gates.
waves.next_action: Start with annual-actual linkage for the anchor whose current plan and annual report share the clearest stable indicator identifiers.

waves.objective: Apply the common record-level quality gate to all non-anchor prefectures without requiring equal record counts where official publication depth differs.
exit_criteria: All 38 prefectures have at least one linked record or a reviewed maximum-source-depth record.
All records preserve missing, unpublished, partial, and not-assessable states without guessing.
waves.next_action: Process regional batches using stable official indicator numbers first, then project and accountability layers where identifiers permit.
